cuts.raw_narration: A wide shot shows a towering, pillar-like stone nest jutting up from jagged rock formations under a cloudy sky, then the camera pushes in with a radial blur. Inside a dark, fleshy womb-like chamber, a clawed silhouette thrashes violently against pink tissue and briefly reveals a monstrous mouth with blunt teeth and a long pink tongue. Squad-leader ants gathered in the cavernous, rib-pillared birthing hall stare upward in shock. A quick cut shows the Royal Guards waiting: one plays a violin, another stands tense, and Neferpitou sits perched on a rock with glowing pink eyes, smiling in anticipation. A giant pulsing green cocoon veined with dark brown is shown in close-up, and the dark, armored figure of the newborn King begins violently tearing his way out of it as a voice announces that the time has come and the king is being born.

In the Queen's dim, fleshy chamber, the giant Chimera Ant Queen lies on her back, wounded and breathing heavily. Colt and the other officer ants stand around her looking devastated — one red octopus-like ant sweats with wide, shocked eyes, and Colt grits his teeth in furious grief. They plead that they need the King's power to heal her, but the newborn King, walking calmly away with the Royal Guards Youpi and Pouf beside him and Neferpitou lingering behind, dismisses her entirely, saying she doesn't matter to them anymore. His tail sways contemptuously as he leaves. Colt stares desperately after them. Neferpitou turns back with a cold, smug smile and rests a pale, cat-like hand on Colt's shoulder, delivering the message that the Queen is no longer needed. Stylized panic-lines flash across Colt's face as he stands in absolute horror while the King and his guards disappear into the tunnel, abandoning the dying Queen.

Outdoors under a cloudy sky, Knuckle, Killua, Gon — with a small pink Nen creature perched on his shoulder — and Shoot stand together on a rocky training ground. The camera cuts between tight close-ups of Gon's tense, tear-filled face and Knuckle's stern profile with the scar on his cheek. Gon, voice breaking, begs him to promise that he will save Kite no matter what. Knuckle listens with a deeply sincere expression and gives his word that he will bring Kite back. He raises a small shogi tile inscribed with a kanji character and holds it up as his oath, swearing on the tile. Gon and Killua watch him quietly, framed from behind as they look up at Knuckle and Shoot standing on towering exposed tree roots, the two boys' solemn profiles closing the moment.

Gon stands motionless with his back to the camera, the small pink Nen beast that has sealed his powers clinging to his shoulder, framed against dark wooden beams. The shot pushes in and cuts to a tight close-up of his face as he finally breaks — tears well up and spill down his cheeks, dripping from his chin, and his mouth twists as he grits his teeth in raw frustration. In flashes he remembers the fight he just lost: a white flash, a counter reading 10320, a solemn Knuckle, Gon rushing him in a burst of light and landing a punch, then the Toritaten Nen beast latching onto Gon's back. The close-up returns as he sobs openly, teeth clenched, tears streaming, saying he never thought being this weak and powerless could be so frustrating. A faint overlay of a worried Killua watching him underscores how helpless his friend feels beside him.

Gon sits curled up in his green jacket with his head buried in his arms, the pink Nen beast still clinging to his back — a picture of complete defeat. The camera moves to Killua standing beside him, looking down with a solemn, protective expression. In close-up Killua's face hardens into quiet determination as he silently vows that for the thirty days Gon cannot use his Nen, he will protect him whatever it takes and keep him safe, and that after that they will go their separate ways. The scene cuts to a wide shot of a covered truck driving off down a dusty road between barren canyon cliffs, carrying the two boys away together.
